prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "Choose your journey to bring your companion to life on your desktop screen."]
1: ["Sign In to Save Your Pet", "Log in with your existing account to preserve your desktop companion and sync preferences across devices."]
2: ["Create Your Custom Pet", "Upload clear photos to generate your custom desktop companion accurately."]
3: ["Name Your Desktop Companion", "Give your pet a unique name to prepare your official desktop adoption certificate.", "Pet Name"]
4: ["Preparing Your Pet", "Your companion is getting ready to land on your desktop screen."]
5: ["Your Pet is Ready!", "Learn how to interact with your pet on your desktop using shortcuts and system tray controls.", "Right-click tray icon to manage settings or hide; press shortcut key to interact."]
6: ["Sign in with your primary account to preserve your desktop pet data and prevent profile resets."]
7: []
8: ["Confirming your certificate registers your pet to your account and prepares it for desktop launch."]
9: ["Desktop Companion Activated", "Your pet is now active on your desktop screen. Enjoy your new companion!"]

verdicts.problem: Specifies primary account type and uses pressure tactics regarding profile resets.
